summary: Microstream resonance causing delayed GPU provisioning and intermittent throughput sag in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer VertexApps reported repeated mid-day throughput drops on their Dedicated GPU pool. Drops present as a sustained ~30-60% throughput sag that recovers after 7-20 minutes but recurs during peak windows. Impact surfaces for low-latency microstreams (many short RPCs < 200ms) driving tail-heavy allocation patterns.

Impact:
- VertexApps reported degraded p50/p95 throughput for production model open/alpha-13B-v1 in us-west-2 during business hours.
- Customer-facing flows saw increased request queueing and request timeouts (rare 504s) during the sag windows.
- Business impact: delayed responses for chat widgets and background scoring batches; customer flagged risk to SLAs.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved capacity for VertexApps (4 x A100 nodes)
- Traffic pattern: many short-lived streams (chat turn RPCs ~80-150ms), bursty at minute granularity
- Platform components implicated: autoscaler and scheduler interactions with resource allocator and attachment pipeline

Observed behavior and metrics:
- sudden drop in served requests/sec for the customer (p10->p50 drop ~35%) when microstream rate crosses ~1200 rps aggregate
- autoscaler increased target nodes but actual GPU attachments lagged by ~5-12 minutes before recovering
- allocator logs show a spike in attach/retry cycles and a burst of ephemeral attach failures with IO wait spikes on network layer
- GPU utilization on existing nodes remains high (~80-95%) while new nodes show delayed attach and NVLink latency spikes
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a dedicated pool with reserved 4 x A100 nodes and pin model open/alpha-13B-v1.
2) Generate many short RPC streams (80-150ms each) from 200 test clients to reach ~1200 rps aggregate for the customer tenant.
3) Observe autoscaler target increases but actual attached GPUs lag; monitor request/sec and queue depth metrics.
4) Reproduce at different burst sizes to validate the microstream threshold behavior.

2026-03-10T14:03:24Z allocator: attach request tenant=vertexapps trace=tx-7f12 retry=1 -> transient-io-error (nvlink-qdepth=128)
2026-03-10T14:10:02Z serving-runtime: stream-accept latency-bump p95 increased from 160ms -> 540ms
observed_metrics: Key graphs attached in console: tenant request/sec (drop at 14:03), attach-retry-rate (spike), allocator-io-wait (spike), autoscale-desired-current-gap (5-12 minutes). NVLink latency traces indicate increased cross-GPU transfer latency during event windows.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: short-lived microstreams are creating high connection churn that starves the orchestrator's attach pipeline; autoscaler over-requests capacity but the attachment pipeline debounces and batches attaches leading to provisioning lag.
Found multiple attach retries correlated with elevated network IO wait on node sidecars; this suggests network path saturation or IO queuing on attach endpoints rather than core GPU exhaustion.
Observed that new nodes are allocated but remain in 'attaching' state longer than normal; root-cause likely at resource-allocator -> attach handshake timeout layer.

Ran targeted simulation in staging: reproduces when microstream median <200ms and per-tenant connection fanout > 1500; increasing stream duration to 400ms removes the failure mode (suggesting backpressure smoothing effect).
Checked related telemetry: no driver crashes, no explicit OOM. NVLink counters show transient queue depth growth aligning with attach windows.
comments: Support (Anita): Opened ticket after initial customer alert. Collected logs and metrics, requested elevated telemetry. (2026-03-10)
SRE (Diego): Prioritizing investigation; allocating time to reproduce in staging and instrument attach pipeline. (2026-03-10)
Customer (VertexApps - Samir R.): Observed slowness mostly between 13:45-15:30 PT yesterday and again today. We rely on chat latency; this is high-impact. (2026-03-10)
Infra (Priya P.): Noted allocator sidecar reported increased syscall latency to attach endpoint; will correlate with node-level dmesg. (2026-03-11)
Runtime (Liam O'Connor): Suggest toggling autoscale debounce window and limiting per-tenant attach parallelism as short-term mitigation. Planning a safe config change. (2026-03-11)
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (temporary config): reduced autoscaler aggressiveness and enabled per-tenant attach throttling to smooth spikes. This reduced attach retry storms and removed the 7-20 minute provisioning lag for VertexApps during the next peak window.

Root cause hypothesis: attachment pipeline was susceptible to 'microstream resonance' — rapid open/close attach patterns caused IO queue amplification and delayed attach completion. Autoscaler increased desired nodes but attachments were bottlenecked by network/sidecar IO behavior causing perceived GPU shortages.

Permanent actions planned: (1) implement attach-path backpressure token-bucket and circuit-breaker in allocator, (2) add autoscaler coordination so desired_nodes is gated by attach-success-rate, (3) improve telemetry of attach latency and NVLink queue metrics, (4) publish runbook for microstream-heavy tenants.
Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/482 fixes attach backpressure and adds metrics. Target rollout to staging 2026-03-18 and prod 2026-03-24 behind a feature flag.
Customer follow-up: informed VertexApps of temporary mitigation and roadmap for permanent fix. Agreed on post-deployment validation window and SLO review.
